source: Water evaporates when heated. Water vapor condenses when cooled. Precipitation returns water to the ground. Water collects in rivers and lakes.

room.title: Weather Station — Teacher Edition
room.mission: The weather station is sealed. Explore the laboratory and archive together, restore its two systems, and reunite their keys at the exit.
room.debrief: Your team restored evaporation and condensation, then reconstructed the cycle that returns water to rivers and lakes.

areas.name: Laboratory
areas.description: A dark diagram and a weather simulator wait for inspection.

areas.name: Archive
areas.description: Field observations reveal the order needed by the cycle mechanism.

nodes.name: UV lens
nodes.description: Investigate uv lens to restore the weather station.
nodes.instruction: Use your team discoveries to restore this part of the station.
hints: Inspect the room for useful evidence.
Combine the field notes with the station diagram.
Use the operating instructions recorded in your journal.

reward.name: UV lens
reward.text: Use this lens on the laboratory wall to reveal the faded operating diagram.

reward.name: Water-cycle notes

reward.name: Operating diagram
reward.text: Chamber A must turn liquid into vapor. Chamber B must turn vapor into droplets. Select the temperature action that causes each change.

nodes.instruction: Use your team discoveries to restore this part of the station.

reward.name: Cycle observations
reward.text: Start when collected water turns into vapor. Clouds form next, then rain falls, and finally water returns to rivers and lakes.

nodes.name: Weather simulator
nodes.description: Investigate weather simulator to restore the weather station.
nodes.instruction: Use your team discoveries to restore this part of the station.
hints: Use the field notes and compare what happens in each chamber.
Chamber A makes vapor; Chamber B makes droplets.
Set Chamber A to Heat and Chamber B to Cool.

reward.name: Simulator key
reward.text: Vapor becomes droplets. The restored simulator releases one half of the exit key.

nodes.learningObjective: Connect temperature changes to evaporation and condensation.
nodes.sourceQuote: Water evaporates when heated. Water vapor condenses when cooled.
nodes.explanation: Heat Chamber A to evaporate water, then cool Chamber B to condense the vapor.

nodes.name: Cycle mechanism
nodes.description: Investigate cycle mechanism to restore the weather station.
nodes.instruction: Use your team discoveries to restore this part of the station.
hints: Compare the ledger with the field notes.
Start with the formation of vapor, then clouds.
Arrange Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, Collection.

reward.name: Cycle key
reward.text: The cycle mechanism starts rotating and releases the second half of the exit key.

nodes.learningObjective: Reconstruct the water cycle from observations.
nodes.sourceQuote: Water evaporates when heated. Water vapor condenses when cooled. Precipitation returns water to the ground. Water collects in rivers and lakes.
nodes.explanation: Evaporation precedes condensation, then precipitation returns water to the ground and collection completes the cycle.

nodes.name: Station exit
nodes.description: Investigate station exit to restore the weather station.
nodes.instruction: Use your team discoveries to restore this part of the station.
hints: Inspect the room for useful evidence.
Combine the field notes with the station diagram.
Use the operating instructions recorded in your journal.

reward.name: Station reopened
reward.text: Both key halves fit. The exit opens and the station can resume its observations.
